headline: Pricing surcharges and a defense-materials deal lift margins
summary_short: NewMarket reported FY2026 Q2 net sales of $747.1M, up 7.0% y/y and 11.6% q/q, with net income of $133.8M (+20.2% y/y) and diluted EPS of $14.54 versus $11.84 a year ago.
summary_long: Petroleum additives net sales rose 3.3% y/y as surcharges tied to Middle East supply-chain raw-material and operating cost disruptions offset a 3.8% worldwide shipment-volume decline; segment gross profit and operating profit rose $7.0M and $9.5M. Specialty materials net sales grew to $67.2M from $42.0M on the Calca hydrazine acquisition plus favorable pricing/mix, lifting segment operating profit to $22.3M from $10.5M. Consolidated operating profit rose 14.3% y/y to $163.7M. Net income grew 20.2% to $133.8M, helped by a lower effective tax rate (21.5% vs 24.7%) on lower foreign taxes. Cash rose to $93.6M; long-term debt fell to $854.8M from $939.6M q/q. Management guided FY2026 total capex to $100-130M.

drivers.explanation: Higher selling prices (Middle East supply-chain surcharges) and the Calca specialty-materials acquisition drove revenue and margin gains, partly offset by lower petroleum additives shipment volumes.

Q2 net sales +7.0% y/y ($48.6M) driven by higher selling prices including Middle East disruption surcharges and specialty materials growth, partially offset by lower worldwide shipment volumes (-3.8%).

Petroleum additives gross profit +$7.0M q2 y/y primarily from the net impact of surcharges implemented in response to higher raw-material and operating costs from Middle East supply-chain disruptions.
Specialty materials operating profit rose to $22.3M from $10.5M on the same pricing/mix and Calca-inclusion factors as net sales, partially offset by higher operating costs.
Tracks operating profit growth plus a lower effective tax rate (21.5% vs 24.7%), which the filing attributes primarily to lower taxes on foreign earnings.
Net income growth combined with a lower weighted-diluted share count (9.159M vs 9.362M a year ago) from ongoing buybacks.
